evidence.basis: PTS S ii 228 and distinctive ordered dung-beetle analogy: pride in dung, monk boasting of food and another invitation plus four requisites, contempt for virtuous monks, long-term harm and concluding training.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Pilahaka Sutta (SN 17.5, PTS S ii 228) matches Mīḷhakasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 161, through the distinctive dung-beetle analogy and the monk’s boasting sequence. evidence.basis: Named Atthakarana/Aḍḍakaraṇa discourse, PTS S i 74, Pasenadi disillusioned by wealthy litigants lying for sensual pleasure, Buddha agrees and ends with fish-in-trap verse.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Atthakarana Sutta (SN 3.7, PTS S i 74) matches Aḍḍakaraṇasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 118. Pasenadi’s judgment complaint, the Buddha’s agreement and the concluding fish-in-a-trap verse establish identity. These edition abbreviations remain unchanged; this is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

evidence.basis: Kosalans forest monk with sensuality, ill-will and harmful thoughts; compassionate forest deity instructs attention, Teacher/Dhamma/Sangha/virtues and joy; monk responds; PTS S i 203.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Ayoniso-manasikara Sutta (SN 9.11, PTS S i 203) matches Akusalavitakkasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 231. The forest monk’s three unskillful thoughts, the deity’s ordered advice and the monk’s final response establish identity despite different titles. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference. Source “See also” material is editorial.

evidence.basis: PTS S i 2, two ordered verses on short life and aging: deva recommends merit, Buddha responds by abandoning worldly bait for peace. Publisher note 1 explicitly attributes expanded introductory framing to SN 1.1.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Upaneyyam Sutta (SN 1.3, PTS S i 2) matches Upanīyasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 3. The deva’s merit verse and the Buddha’s contrasting renunciation verse identify this dialogue. Walshe’s note 1 explicitly says the longer introduction repeats SN 1.1’s framing; VRI SN 1.3 keeps a short Savatthi introduction. This is not line-by-line alignment or an expansion of bundled Pāli. The numbered Notes section is the translator’s explanation, not canonical speech. This page is not a translation of SN 1.1.

evidence.basis: PTS S ii 18, three distinctions (teacher, practitioner, liberation) concerning aging-and-death then the dependent-origination sequence through ignorance. Same-named SN 22.115 instead concerns five aggregates.

links.mapping_note: Publisher’s whole-discourse version with repetitions condensed: ATI Dhammakathiko Sutta (SN 12.16, PTS S ii 18) matches Dhammakathikasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 16. Teaching, practising and liberation concern aging-and-death and then the dependent-origination sequence through ignorance, unlike the aggregates in same-named SN 22.115. ATI condenses the repeated sequence into a bracketed summary; VRI also abbreviates but lists its intermediate links. This is not line-by-line alignment or a fully expanded rendering of every repeated clause. The bracketed summary and numbered Notes are translator/editorial material; bundled Pāli stays unchanged.

evidence.basis: Ananda asks Buddha to visit the water-purity brahman; evening/morning washing claim; Dhamma lake/virtue ford stanza; lay refuge ending. PTS S i 182.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sangaarava Sutta (SN 7.21, PTS S i 182) matches Saṅgāravasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 207. Ananda’s invitation, the brahman’s twice-daily purification claim, lake/ford verse and lay refuge ending establish identity. ATI condenses travel/greeting details and uses bracketed stage directions, an SN 7.1 cross-reference and a numbered explanatory Note. VRI also abbreviates its closing formula. These are publisher/editorial conventions, not newly generated Pāli; this is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Five clinging aggregates; arising/ceasing, gratification, danger and escape understood as they are; stream-entry assurance. PTS S iii 160. Adjacent 110 instead describes arahant release.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sotaapanno Sutta (SN 22.109, PTS S iii 160) matches Sotāpannasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 109. Knowledge of five aspects of the five clinging aggregates ends in the stream-enterer description, distinct from the arahant conclusion in SN 22.110. ATI lists aggregates VRI abbreviates; its bracketed setup and numbered Note are editorial. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Five aspects of clinging aggregates; liberation without clinging; completed-life, laid-down-burden, highest-goal and destroyed-fetters formula. PTS S iii 161; distinct from 109 stream-entry ending.

links.mapping_note: Publisher’s whole-discourse version with an abbreviated opening: ATI Araham Sutta (SN 22.110, PTS S iii 161) matches Arahantasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 110. Its “As above” opening points to SN 22.109 for the shared setup; this reader does not silently fetch or splice that page. The release-without-clinging and completed-arahant formula identify SN 22.110, not SN 22.109 or other Arahant-titled texts. The numbered Note is editorial; this is not line-by-line alignment or a fully expanded standalone opening.

evidence.basis: Five aggregates as clingable phenomena, each paired with desire/passion as clinging; opening and concluding definitions. PTS S iii 167.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Upadana Sutta (SN 22.121, PTS S iii 167) matches Upādāniyasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 121. Form, feeling, perception, fabrications and consciousness are paired with desire-passion as clinging. ATI spells out repetitions VRI abbreviates with …pe…; both editions’ source text stays unchanged. This is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

evidence.basis: Feeling born of six contacts is impermanent/changeable; faith-follower, Dhamma-follower, stream-enterer formula. PTS S iii 226; unabridged classification formula checked in VRI SN 25.1.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Vedana Sutta (SN 25.5, PTS S iii 226) matches Samphassajāsuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 306. Feelings born of six contacts identify this unit. evidence.basis: Instruction to be mindful and clearly comprehending; four mindfulness domains then feelings, thoughts and perceptions known arising/persisting/ending; repeated instruction. PTS S v 180.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sata Sutta (SN 47.35, PTS S v 180) matches indexed Satisutta, VRI paragraph 401. This sequence and the repeated instruction distinguish it from similarly titled mindfulness texts. Both editions abbreviate repeated domains; this is not line-by-line alignment or numbering-only inference.

evidence.basis: Moggallana signless concentration, sign-following consciousness, Buddha intervention, restored concentration and final teacher-supported attainment. Complete quoted unit; introductory earlier-eight summary and eight Notes are editorial.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Animitto Sutta (SN 40.9, PTS S iv 268) matches Animittapañhāsuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 340. evidence.basis: Five aggregates, four self-relations, change and ensuing worry versus instructed disciple without self-identification/worry; both mirrored sections complete in condensed form. PTS S iii 15.

links.english_title: The Discourse on the Orderliness of the Dhamma

evidence.basis: Whether Tathagatas arise or not: stability of Dhamma; all formations impermanent, all formations suffering, all phenomena not-self; each followed by awakening/declaration formula. PTS A i 286.

evidence.basis: Five losses and corresponding five successes: relatives, wealth, health, virtue, views; distinction of first three from final two regarding bad/good rebirth. PTS A iii 147.

evidence.basis: Three trainings: virtue, four jhanas, ending fermentations and direct release, followed by five training stanzas and flame/unbinding conclusion.

evidence.basis: Four unsuitable wilderness qualities (sensual/hostile/harmful thought and weak discernment) contrasted with their four suitable opposites; both sections match.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Arannika Sutta (AN 4.259, PTS A ii 252) matches indexed AN 4.262 (Araññasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 262. The unsuitable/suitable thought-and-discernment contrasts establish identity, not a general +3 rule. Bracketed glosses and “See also” references are publisher/editorial material. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Female noble disciple grows in faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom; female lay-disciple verse. Adjacent 5.63 concerns male disciple.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Vuddhi Sutta (AN 5.64, PTS A iii 80) matches Dutiyavaḍḍhisuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 64. Its female noble disciple, five growth qualities and female lay-disciple verse distinguish it from the neighboring male-disciple AN 5.63. This is not line-by-line alignment or a title/number-only inference.

evidence.basis: Perception of impermanence in all formations; six ordered rewards from instability to foremost contemplative qualities. Distinct from 6.104 not-self list.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Anodhi Sutta (AN 6.102, PTS A iii 443) matches Anavatthitasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 102. Impermanence in formations and six ordered rewards identify this version, not the similarly titled not-self discourse AN 6.104. The fetter Note and “See also” references are editorial, not additional coverage. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Not-self perception in all phenomena; non-identification, ending I-making/my-making, uncommon knowledge, seeing cause and causally arisen phenomena. Last two combined in English sentence.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Anodhi Sutta (AN 6.104, PTS A iii 444) matches Atammayasuttaṃ, VRI paragraph 104. Its not-self perception, non-identification and I/my-making list distinguish it from AN 6.102. English combines seeing cause and causally originated phenomena in one sentence; both final items remain represented. The uncommon-knowledge Note is commentary interpretation, not canonical speech. This is not line-by-line alignment.

links.english_title: Conditions for No Decline Among the Monks

evidence.basis: Rajagaha Vulture Peak; seven monastic conditions: frequent/harmonious meetings, training rules, elders, craving, wilderness, welcoming good companions; conclusion.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Bhikkhu-aparihaniya Sutta (AN 7.21, PTS A iv 21) maps to indexed AN 7.23 (Paṭhamasattakasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 23. ATI’s bracketed numerals label the list; this is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Radiant deity reports seven respects ending shame and compunction; departure and two stanzas. Distinct from heedfulness-centered neighboring text.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Hirima Sutta (AN 7.32, PTS A iv 28) maps to indexed AN 7.33 (Hirigāravasutta), VRI paragraph 33. The deity’s seven respects ending shame/compunction and two final stanzas establish identity. ATI specifies three circuits at departure; VRI states circumambulation without a count. Editorial cross-references retain ATI numbering. This is not line-by-line alignment or a general offset rule.

evidence.basis: Four mirrored sections: woman/man attending inward to own sex traits and outward to others, followed by corresponding non-bondage contrasts and conclusion.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence with edition numbering: ATI Sannoga Sutta (AN 7.48, PTS A iv 57) maps to indexed AN 7.51 (Saṃyogasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 51. Four mirrored woman/man bondage and non-bondage sections identify the discourse. ATI condenses repeated negative lists; VRI abbreviates part of its introduction. This is not line-by-line alignment or a general +3 rule.

evidence.basis: Anathapindika; unguarded/guarded mind, bodily/verbal/mental actions, sogginess/rot and bad/good death; parallel poorly/well-roofed house similes.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Kuta Sutta AN 3.105 maps to indexed AN 3.109 (Arakkhitasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 110. Anathapindika, the guarded/unguarded action sequences and both roof similes establish correspondence, not the overlapping PTS page or a general offset. Nearby AN 3.107 concerns singing/dancing, AN 3.108 insatiability. ATI abbreviates repeated action lists; editorial See also retains publisher numbering. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Four jhanas; eleven ways of regarding the five aggregates; Pure Abodes rebirth not shared by ordinary people.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Jhana Sutta AN 4.124 matches indexed AN 4.124 (Dutiyanānākaraṇasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 124. The four absorptions, eleven contemplation predicates and Pure Abodes conclusion identify the second discourse. Both editions abbreviate repeated absorption formulas. These published abbreviations are retained, not filled in by the tool. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Maha Kotthita questions Sariputta; four alternatives after six contact-media cease, each rejected; mutual extent and cessation of elaboration.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Kotthita Sutta AN 4.174 maps to indexed AN 4.173 (Mahākoṭṭhikasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 173. The named interlocutors, four rejected alternatives and contact-media/elaboration conclusion establish identity. English condenses repeated questions and adds bracketed glosses, speaker labels and an editorial Note; these are not extra canonical passages. No general minus-one rule is inferred. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Nadika Brick Hall; colt/thoroughbred grain and spur similes, five hindrances, eleven dependencies, three occurrences of the homage stanza and perception explanation.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sandha Sutta AN 11.10 maps to indexed AN 11.9 (Saddhasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 9. The Brick Hall setting, colt/thoroughbred contrasts, hindrance/dependency lists, three homage occurrences and concluding perception explanation establish whole-discourse correspondence. ATI calls the interlocutor Sandha; VRI uses Saddha. Both use stock-list abbreviations. The two Notes are editorial glosses, not additional canonical text. No general minus-one rule is inferred. This is not line-by-line alignment. Source wording caution: in its positive thoroughbred section ATI says “obsessed with uncertainty”, while VRI has na vicikicchāparetena (not obsessed with uncertainty). The published English is preserved, not silently corrected; the two wordings are not equivalent.

evidence.basis: Two bright guardians hiri/ottappa; kinship/respect relationships and animal promiscuity counterfactual, ending with preserved distinctions.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Lokapala Sutta AN 2.9 matches indexed AN 2.9 (Cariyasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 9. The two bright qualities, kinship/respect relationships and animal counterfactual identify the whole discourse. English conscience/concern are translator renderings of hirī/ottappa; the explanatory Note and See also are editorial, not extra canonical scope. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Both unskillful-abandoning and skillful-developing sections; possibility argument and harm/pain versus benefit/pleasure conditionals.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Kusala Sutta AN 2.19 matches indexed AN 2.19, VRI paragraph 19. Both abandoning the unskillful and developing the skillful, their possibility arguments and harm/benefit conditionals establish whole-text identity. Indexed title Adhikaraṇavaggo is the containing chapter label, not an inferred independent sutta title. See also references are editorial. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Two reciprocal misrepresentations: treating inferential meaning as explicit and explicit meaning as inferential.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Neyyatha Sutta AN 2.25 maps to indexed AN 2.24, VRI paragraph 25. The reciprocal neyyattha/nītattha misrepresentation contrasts establish identity, not the shared PTS page or a general offset. Indexed title Bālavaggo is the containing chapter label. The publisher reference remains AN 2.25. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Autobiographical luxury, three aging/illness/death reflections, three intoxications with misconduct and monk reversion, five closing verse groups.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sukhamala Sutta AN 3.38 maps as a complete combined page to indexed AN 3.39 (Sukhumālasuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 39. The publisher note explains its PTS III.38/III.39 split at the triple asterisk; both parts belong to this one VRI unit. Luxury, three reflections, intoxication/misconduct and monk-reversion sections, and closing verses establish scope; indexed AN 3.38 is instead the Sakka uposatha discourse. Source wording caution: the English closing verse begins “Subject to birth”, whereas VRI begins Byādhidhammā (subject to illness). Preserve both published readings without silent correction. Translator note and See also are editorial. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: More than150 rules and three trainings; four accomplishments yielding stream-winner, once-returner, non-returner, arahant; partial/full conclusion.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sekhin Sutta AN 3.85 maps to indexed AN 3.86 (Paṭhamasikkhāsuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 87. More-than-150 rules, three trainings, four ordered accomplishment/outcome sections and final partial/full conclusion distinguish it from indexed AN 3.85’s short learner inquiry and verses and AN 3.87’s expanded rebirth subclasses. The two Notes, including the historical rule-count discussion and AN 3.88 cross-reference, are editorial; no extra alignment is inferred. This is not line-by-line alignment.

evidence.basis: Same rules/trainings frame; seven-times/family-to-family/one-seed/once-returner and five nonreturner categories; final arahant and partial/full conclusion.

links.mapping_note: Whole-discourse correspondence: ATI Sekhin Sutta AN 3.86 maps to indexed AN 3.87 (Dutiyasikkhāsuttaṃ), VRI paragraph 88. Explicit stream-entry rebirth subclasses and five non-returner subclasses distinguish this second training text from indexed AN 3.86.
